title: These 40-something founders say they have something the AI kids don't
excerpt: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan declared the "age of the unc." We asked founders in their 40s whether what's old is new again.
content_html:
Amir Elaguizy has books about neural networks from the '60s.

The 42-year-old serial entrepreneur doesn't believe that being younger means you're more AI-native. Elaguizy emailed with Geoffrey Hinton, the "Godfather of AI," before Hinton started working at Google. He's been learning about AI's roots for decades.

"For me, AI is a continuum," he said. "I watched it the whole time. It's not like it came online for me in 2022."

For Elaguizy, his age is a perk. It's a sign to investors that he's serious and knows how to build a business. (Elaguizy sold his first company to Zynga in 2011.) It also shows that he's dogged, he said, and not taking his earlier cash-out and retiring.

These days, his age cohort wants in. Elaguizy said that many of his friends were coming out of retirement to launch new AI startups. "You have all these old guys who are not just back at it, but back at the keyboard, typing code," he said.

Elaguizy called it a "vibe shift," something Garry Tan would likely agree with. The Y Combinator CEO posted that we were entering an "age of the unc." ("Unc," for those unfamiliar with Gen Z parlance, is a shortening of "uncle" to call someone old.) Tan expected a new class of unicorn founders in their 40s.

The founder in their 40s with taste and discernment is the new gentleman unicorn founder

Because there can be 100x to 1000x of them working at their beck and call via agents and software factories all the time https://t.co/VV5GOgI12h

— Garry Tan (@garrytan) July 5, 2026

It's a bit ironic, given Y Combinator's declining average founder age. In 2025, one cohort had an average age of 24. That's a hallmark of the AI era: founders in their early 20s who pop Zyns and troll on X. Indeed, Business Insider once called it a "youthquake."

But these founders say that their age is a benefit, not a bug.

'The age of the unc'

Michal Cieplinski described AI as a reset — one that affected both older and younger founders.

"We had to learn Claude Code at the same time," he said. "It's not like a 21-year-old kid had a start on me. No! We all had the same starting point."

Cieplinski is the 48-year-old founder of HiJenny, an AI home manager. He referenced the internet discourse about "taste." The thinking goes: in the age of AI, technical skills will be less important than your sense of judgment.

With age, you have a better sense of taste, Cieplinski said. "I'd add to it: with age, you have persistence."

Are older founders actually experiencing a renaissance? Throughout my chats, founders pointed to the ages of the CEOs of the AI labs. Sam Altman is 41. Dario Amodei is 43. They're not college dropouts sleeping on futons.

Stanford University's Venture Capital Initiative compared the average age at founding between a random sample and unicorns, or companies worth over $1 billion. The average age of a unicorn founder was 39.9 in the 2020s, compared with 35 in the random sample.

The average founding age of a unicorn is also going up: in the 2010s, it was 35.4.

Even if the data suggests older founders are more closely associated with unicorn status, it's not clear that investors are eager to bet on them.

Ismail Pelaseyed, the 40-year-old cofounder of the cybersecurity startup Superagent, said he felt the push in Silicon Valley: "You have to be young, straight out of Harvard or Stanford."

Pelaseyed was 39 when he went through Y Combinator. He said he felt like a father to many of his ultra-young batchmates.

"I think that most venture capitalists want someone young, because it takes a long time to build something big," he said. After all, Mark Zuckerberg was 19 when het met Peter Thiel, Facebook's first outside investor.

Elaguizy disagrees. Sure, there's lots of money in the AI market right now, opening doors for founders with little experience. But what about when the going gets rough?

"In an environment where capital is less free, us old guys are a little bit more attractive," he said.

Does age equal experience?

Both of Carmen Li's jobs require deep technical experience.

Li is the 40-year-old CEO of two GPU-related businesses: Compute Exchange and Silicon Data. While a 20-year-old may be able to kick-start a social app — especially with the ease of modern AI tools — it's harder to work on the compute side, she said.

Still, that doesn't mean she benefits from her age. Li said that she benefits from her experience — and that the two aren't necessarily tied.

"You can be a 40-year-old who's done nothing with your life," she said. "You'll be a worse startup founder than a 20-year-old. 40 is just a number."

There's one demographic that Li said did particularly well in their 40s: women.

Many women founders leave the industry in their 30s to have kids, Li said, before returning to entrepreneurship in their 40s. (Li also clocked the subtle gendering in Tan's post, which referenced the "gentleman unicorn founder.")

Mo Shaikh is a fan of older founders, precisely because of their experience. "They draw from all these lessons that they've learned," he said.

That doesn't mean that they're serial entrepreneurs, the 40-year-old cofounder and general partner of Maximum Frequency Venture said. Rather, he's looking for people with deep technical knowledge in their field.

"There are many founders out there that don't know that they're founders yet," he said.

The founders I spoke to quibbled about whether it was a better or worse time to be a mid-40s entrepreneur. Li said it's always been a good time to be older. "They're just not the sexy story," she said. "They're regular people."

But Elaguizy was firm about his "vibe shift." The industry was embracing a "what's old is new again" mentality, he said.

"For every 22-year-old in a hoodie, I'm seeing a couple of 40-year-olds not in hoodies," he said.

content_html_zh:
Amir Elaguizy 拥有 60 年代有关神经网络的书籍。

这位 42 岁的连续创业者并不认为年轻就意味着更擅长人工智能。 在 Hinton 开始在谷歌工作之前，Elaguizy 曾与“人工智能教父”Geoffrey Hinton 发过电子邮件。 几十年来，他一直在研究人工智能的根源。

“对我来说，人工智能是一个连续体，”他说。 “我一直看着它。 这对我来说并不是 2022 年才上线的。”

对于埃拉吉齐来说，他的年龄是一种优势。 这向投资者表明他是认真的并且知道如何建立一家企业。 （Elaguizy 于 2011 年将他的第一家公司卖给了 Zynga。） 他说，这也表明他很顽强，没有拿走之前的现金并退休。

如今，他的同龄人想要加入。 Elaguizy 表示，他的许多朋友即将复出，创办新的人工智能初创公司。 “所有这些老家伙不仅回到了电脑前，而且回到了键盘上，输入代码，”他说。

埃拉吉兹称之为“氛围转变”，加里·谭可能会同意这一点。 Y Combinator 首席执行官表示，我们正在进入“UNC 时代”。 （对于那些不熟悉 Z 世代用语的人来说，“Unc”是“叔叔”的缩写，用来称呼某人老。） Tan 预计会有 40 多岁的新一类独角兽创始人。

40多岁有品味和洞察力的创始人是新绅士独角兽创始人因为可能有100倍到1000倍的人一直通过代理和软件工厂听命于他们 https://t.co/VV5GOgI12h - Garry Tan (@garrytan) 2026年7月5日

考虑到 Y Combinator 创始人的平均年龄不断下降，这有点讽刺。 2025 年，一组人的平均年龄为 24 岁。 这是人工智能时代的一个标志：20 岁出头的创始人就流行 Zyns 并在 X 上进行攻击。 事实上，《商业内幕》曾称其为“青年地震”。

但这些创始人表示，年龄是一个优势，而不是一个缺陷。

“北卡罗来纳大学的时代”

Michal Cieplinski 将人工智能描述为一种重置——一种对年长和年轻创始人都产生影响的重置。

“我们必须同时学习克劳德密码，”他说。 “这不像是一个 21 岁的孩子对我下手。 不！ 我们都有相同的起点。”

48 岁的 Cieplinski 是人工智能家庭管家 HiJenny 的创始人。 他引用了互联网上关于“品味”的讨论。 人们的想法是：在人工智能时代，判断力比技术技能更重要。

切普林斯基说，随着年龄的增长，你的味觉会变得更好。 “我想补充一点：随着年龄的增长，你会有毅力。”

老创始人真的正在经历复兴吗？ 在我的聊天中，创始人们指出了人工智能实验室首席执行官的年龄。 萨姆·奥尔特曼 41 岁。 达里奥·阿莫代 43 岁。 他们不是睡在蒲团上的大学辍学者。

斯坦福大学的风险投资计划对随机样本和独角兽公司（或价值超过 10 亿美元的公司）的平均创立年龄进行了比较。 2020 年代独角兽创始人的平均年龄为 39.9 岁，而随机样本中的平均年龄为 35 岁。

独角兽公司的平均创立年龄也在上升：2010年代为35.4岁。

即使数据表明年长的创始人与独角兽地位的联系更紧密，但尚不清楚投资者是否愿意押注于他们。

网络安全初创公司 Superagent 的 40 岁联合创始人伊斯梅尔·佩拉塞耶德 (Ismail Pelaseyed) 表示，他感受到了硅谷的推动力：“你必须很年轻，直接从哈佛或斯坦福大学毕业。”

Pelaseyed 加入 Y Combinator 时年仅 39 岁。 他说，对于许多超年轻的队友来说，他感觉就像父亲一样。

“我认为大多数风险投资家都想要年轻的人，因为建立大的东西需要很长时间，”他说。 毕竟，马克·扎克伯格 (Mark Zuckerberg) 遇见 Facebook 第一位外部投资者彼得·泰尔 (Peter Thiel) 时才 19 岁。

埃拉吉齐不同意。 当然，目前人工智能市场上有很多资金，为缺乏经验的创始人打开了大门。 但当事情变得艰难时怎么办？

“在资本不太自由的环境中，我们这些老家伙更具吸引力，”他说。

年龄等于经验吗？

Carmen Li 的两项工作都需要深厚的技术经验。

40 岁的李是两家 GPU 相关企业的首席执行官：Compute Exchange 和 Silicon Data。 她说，虽然 20 岁的人可能能够启动社交应用程序——尤其是借助现代人工智能工具的便利——但在计算方面工作却更加困难。

尽管如此，这并不意味着她会从她的年龄中受益。 李说，她从自己的经历中受益匪浅，而且两者没有必然联系。

“你可以成为一个 40 岁的人，却什么也没做，”她说。 “你会成为一个比 20 岁年轻人更糟糕的初创公司创始人。 40只是一个数字。”

李说，有一个人群在 40 多岁的时候表现尤其出色：女性。

李说，许多女性创始人在 30 多岁时离开这个行业去生孩子，然后在 40 多岁时重返创业。 （李还在谭的帖子中提到了“绅士独角兽创始人”中微妙的性别划分。）

Mo Shaikh 是老创始人的粉丝，正是因为他们的经验。 “他们从他们学到的所有这些教训中吸取了教训，”他说。

这位 40 岁的 MaximumFrequency Venture 联合创始人兼普通合伙人表示，这并不意味着他们是连续创业者。 相反，他正在寻找在各自领域拥有深厚技术知识的人。

“有很多创始人还不知道自己是创始人，”他说。

我采访过的创始人对于对于 40 多岁的企业家来说现在是更好还是更坏的时代存在争议。 李说，变老总是一个好时机。 “他们只是不性感的故事，”她说。 “他们是普通人。”

但埃拉吉齐对他的“氛围转变”态度坚定。 他说，这个行业正在拥抱一种“旧的又是新的”的心态。

他说：“我看到每一个 22 岁的人都穿着连帽衫，而另外两个 40 岁的人则不穿连帽衫。”
